title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-17
content:
Quick notes from on-call shift (17 Mar 2026) - personal scratchpad

Summary:
- PD page: PD-4371 (high 95p latency on hosted-api/complete route) triggered at ~09:18 UTC.
- Impact: elevated tail latency for text-completion calls (~95th went from 420ms->1.6s).
- Root-cause (working hypothesis): sudden spike in KV cache miss rate after rollout of kv-cache change in serving-runtime PR #876 -> cache warming behaviour + increased cold-start tokenization cost on small model variants.

Timeline / actions taken:
- 09:18 PD alerted (pager duty). Slack: #oncall-team pinged.
- 09:19 Looked at grafana: hosted-api/complete 95p jump from 420ms to ~1.6s across us-east-1 region.
  - Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/latency-overview
  - Saw concurrent spike in kv_cache_miss_rate and model_loads/sec for gpt-small-001.
- 09:22 Ran quick curl to /health and /metrics on a few hosts (kubectl port-forward to service): good. No OOM.
- 09:25 Checked recent deploys: serving-runtime v2.11.3 rolled at 08:55 UTC (canary -> gradual) with kv cache optimization change (PR #876).
- 09:30 Scoped: traffic split shows >60% of requests still on primary models; however canary nodes showed 3x model_loads/sec against baseline.
- 09:35 Mitigation: rolled back serving-runtime to v2.11.2 for canary pool (kubectl set image on deployment hosted-api-canary -> rollback). Observed 95p latency start to trend down after ~2 mins.
- 09:50 Incident declared: degraded performance (severity: SEV2). Notify CS and product.
- 10:05 Confirmed rollback reduced kv_cache_miss_rate to baseline; 95p latency back to ~450ms in us-east-1.
- 10:20 Monitoring: set temporary alert thresholds to detect quick spikes in model_loads/sec and kv_cache_miss_rate.

Commands I ran (notes):
- kubectl -n hosted get pods -l app=hosted-api -o wide
- kubectl logs hosted-api-canary-5f7b -c runtime --since=10m | grep -i "kv cache miss"
- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache_miss_rate
- curl -sS https://hosted-api.redwood.ai/v1/complete -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"gpt-small-001","input":"healthcheck"}'

What I observed:
- Canary nodes had repeated model load events (model_loads/sec spiked). Looks like a logic path introduced in PR #876 that invalidates local prefix cache too aggressively for certain tokenization patterns (short prompts + many concurrent different prompts).
- The median latency didn't change much; tail was affected (95p+). That matches increased cold-starts / KV misses rather than global overload.
- No memory leaks or pod restarts. CPU utilisation on GPUs normal.

Runbook TODOs / follow-ups (me + engineering):
- [ ] Create small postmortem note in Confluence and link PD timeline -> assign to me (Taylor). (Confluence page template: ENG-INCIDENTS)
- [ ] Add a regression test for prefix caching behaviour with mixed short prompts (unit/integration in serving-runtime tests). POC branch: refs in linked artifacts. (owner: Lena)
- [ ] Update runbook section "prefix cache warmup" with explicit checks and alert thresholds for kv_cache_miss_rate and model_loads/sec. (owner: Taylor)
- [ ] Add a Grafana panel for model_loads/sec by model variant and region (owner: Observability).
- [ ] Add automated canary guard: if model_loads/sec > X for 5m, pause rollout and alert (owner: release-engineering).
- [ ] Follow up with product about customer-facing message for any customers impacted (owner: CS).

Notes for postmortem (short):
- Trigger: rollout of serving-runtime change that changed cache invalidation policy (PR #876).
- Effect: increased cache miss rate on canary nodes -> more model loads -> tail latency spikes.
- Why not caught earlier: insufficient load diversity in canary traffic (mostly homogenous prompts), missed mixed-prompt patterns in canary tests.
- Proposed fixes: revert change (done), add more varied canary traffic profile, add test coverage + telemetry.

Outstanding items I left in my head / next shift handoff:
- Ensure rollback stays in place until PR #876 is updated and reviewed with additional tests.
- Double-check that rollback didn't cascade into dedicated customers (notify ops for Dedicated cluster).
- Confirm alert docs are linked in runbook and that on-call playbook lists the exact metrics and threshold values.

Random scratch TODOs (personal):
- Draft the Confluence incident note (30-45min).
- Ping release-engineering to discuss implementing the canary guard.
- Add a snippet to runbook for quick rollback commands (kubectl set image / k8s rollout undo) with exact deployment names (shortcuts).

Relevant tickets / links to include in postmortem:
- PD-4371 (PagerDuty)
- ENG-1024 (tracking postmortem and follow-ups)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/876
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api/latency-overview
- Runbook page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+Prefix+Cache

End of shift notes:
- Logged postmortem stub. Set reminders for follow-ups.
- Shift handoff to Lena at 17:50 UTC. Left the list above and pinned links in #oncall-handoff Slack thread.

-- Taylor
